entries.summary: A concealed Pung-based hand in one suit, with the exact winning/provenance conditions owned by the rules treatment.
entries.whatItIs: A reviewed BMJA/Outside-the-Box special built from four concealed Pungs and a concealed pair in one numbered suit, with optional honours where the shared predicate permits them.
entries.whatItMeans: The hand uses ordinary grouped sets, but concealment and how the hand is completed are part of the special's qualification rather than just its visible tile composition.
entries.whySpecial: All four melds are concealed Pungs and the hand is constrained to one suited family with the shared Buried Treasure provenance rules.

entries.summary: A non-East player wins with East's first discard.
entries.whatItIs: A BMJA event-defined special tied to the first discard made by East.
entries.whatItMeans: The hand shape can be ordinary; the special comes from the exact moment and discarder that provide the winning tile.
entries.whySpecial: Mahjong is completed immediately from East's first discard before normal play has developed.
entries.referenceNote: Keep the current BMJA event-evidence mapping and provenance status attached; do not generalise this definition to other profiles from name similarity alone.

entries.displayName: Gathering the Plum Blossom from the Roof
entries.summary: A replacement draw produces 5 Circles and that tile completes Mahjong.
entries.whatItIs: A BMJA event-defined special where the winning replacement tile is specifically 5 Circles.
entries.whatItMeans: The final hand shape alone is not enough; the scorer needs to know that 5 Circles arrived as the qualifying replacement draw.
entries.whySpecial: Both the winning tile identity and the replacement-draw event are part of qualification.

evidenceBindings.locator: Event-dependent specials — Gathering the Plum Blossom from the Roof

entries.displayName: Plucking the Moon from the Bottom of the Sea
entries.summary: The last drawable live-wall tile is 1 Circles and it completes Mahjong.
entries.whatItIs: A BMJA event-defined special where the winning tile is specifically 1 Circles drawn as the last live-wall tile.
entries.whatItMeans: Qualification depends on both tile identity and wall position; an identical final hand reached another way is not this event treatment.
entries.whySpecial: The hand wins on a named tile at the final live-wall draw.

evidenceBindings.locator: Event-dependent specials — Plucking the Moon from the Bottom of the Sea

entries.summary: Buzzard 2000 treats All Winds and Dragons as a configured limit hand; the current executable treatment uses only honour Pungs/Kongs and a pair.
entries.whatItIs: A Buzzard 2000 named limit treatment using the current canonical All Winds and Dragons predicate.
entries.whatItMeans: Under the executable treatment, every set and the pair are Winds or Dragons; no suited tiles appear.
entries.whySpecial: Buzzard lists All Winds and Dragons among its ten limit hands, irrespective of ordinary score value.
entries.referenceNote: This is presented as the current executable Buzzard treatment. Do not use this learner entry as independent historical proof that every other ruleset's All Winds and Dragons is equivalent.

evidenceBindings.locator: §B Winner only — All Winds and Dragons; §D Limit hands item 1

entries.summary: Three Wind Pungs/Kongs with the fourth Wind as the pair plus another set; Buzzard also allows a related non-winning limit case that the current winning-only detector cannot represent.
entries.whatItIs: A Buzzard Four-Wind-family limit treatment with a known source/runtime boundary.
entries.whatItMeans: The current executable detector recognises a complete winning form, but Buzzard's source also allows this Wind-family limit to score against other losers while incomplete/non-winning.
entries.whySpecial: The hand centres all four Wind identities and has an exceptional Buzzard settlement rule beyond ordinary winner-only special-hand scoring.
entries.referenceNote: The example is a current-runtime winning form only. It is not exhaustive source qualification until the non-winner limit seam is represented in the knowledge/runtime model.

entries.summary: Mahjong is made with East Wind's first discard.
entries.whatItIs: A Buzzard configured-limit event treatment tied to East's first discard.
entries.whatItMeans: The completed hand does not define the special by itself; the winning tile must be East's first discard.
entries.whySpecial: Buzzard lists this immediate first-discard win among its ten limit hands.
entries.referenceNote: Keep this as Buzzard-local teaching; #351 did not prove full cross-profile equivalence with BMJA Earth's Blessing from the shared pattern ID alone.

entries.summary: Buzzard's current executable limit treatment is a grouped hand made only from suited 1s and 9s.
entries.whatItIs: A Buzzard configured-limit treatment bound to the current all-terminal suited Pung/Kong-and-pair predicate.
entries.whatItMeans: Only suited 1s and 9s appear in the executable hand shape; Winds and Dragons are not part of this treatment.
entries.whySpecial: Buzzard lists All Ones and Nines among its ten limit hands.
entries.referenceNote: Keep the Buzzard local name and configured-limit treatment distinct from the score/value treatments used by other profiles even where the executable structure matches.

evidenceBindings.locator: heads-and-tails / local name All Ones and Nines

entries.summary: Four concealed Pungs/Kongs plus a pair.
entries.whatItIs: A Buzzard limit hand whose four melds are concealed Pungs or Kongs.
entries.whatItMeans: The grouped structure is ordinary, but every meld must satisfy the concealed Pung/Kong condition represented by the current detector.
entries.whySpecial: Buzzard does not use a generic concealed-hand ordinary double here; concealed Pungs/Kongs are one of its named limit hands.

evidenceBindings.locator: §D Limit hands item 7; §B remove generic fully-concealed ordinary double

entries.summary: East wins a thirteenth consecutive Mahjong while remaining East.
entries.whatItIs: A Buzzard configured-limit event treatment based on a long consecutive sequence of East wins.
entries.whatItMeans: Qualification is table-history context, not a particular final tile pattern; the scorer needs the fact that this is East's thirteenth consecutive Mahjong.
entries.whySpecial: It rewards an exceptional sequence across many hands rather than a single hand composition.
